title: The Credit Stack Attack: How I Build Six Figures in Unsecured Credit
actionable_recommendations: Have a FICO score of at least 700 to access unsecured credit.
Form a corporate entity (preferably a C corporation) in Wyoming or Delaware for anonymity.
Obtain an EIN for your corporation during the formation process.
Consider S corporation election by filing IRS Form 2553.
Open a business bank account as soon as your corporate entity is created.
Apply for business credit cards with your new corporate entity.
Use business credit cards responsibly to build credit over time.
Consider forming multiple corporations for stacking credit limits.
Establish a business relationship with Navy Federal Credit Union.
Start with a small business line of credit and gradually increase the limit.
claims_requiring_current_verification: Access to up to $150,000 in unsecured credit is possible within 30 days.
Requires a minimum FICO score of around 700 to be eligible for certain credit.
Corporation formation services may vary in their capability and fees.
Navy Federal Credit Union requires a year of relationship to apply for business credit.
Wells Fargo can provide a minimum of a $10,000 business line of credit.
intended_organization_or_user: Individuals looking to build substantial access to unsecured credit for business purposes.
major_ideas: The 'Credit Stack Attack' strategy for acquiring unsecured credit.
Importance of good credit and corporate structure in accessing business financing.
Utilizing anonymous corporations to protect personal information.
Building credit through multiple corporate entities.
prerequisites: Good personal credit score (preferably mid-FICO score of 700 or higher).
Formation of a corporate entity with an EIN.
Funding a business bank account immediately after opening.
proposed_workflow: Form a corporate entity using a reliable service.
Obtain an EIN during the formation process.
File IRS Form 2553 to elect S corporation status.
Consider forming additional corporate entities for credit stacking.
Establish relationships with banks for business lines of credit.
tools_templates_resources: Legal and financial resources for forming corporations (e.g., wyomingcompany.com).
QuickBooks for invoicing and obtaining credit offers.
